attachments.insertion_landmark: outer surface of the rib below, between the tubercle and the angle

actions: assist rotation and lateral flexion of the trunk

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: One of the few thoracic muscles supplied by dorsal rami rather than intercostal nerves.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Linear probe transverse (axial) at the target thoracic level, identifying the transverse process, the rib, and the pleura at the depth of the paravertebral space; needle advanced in-plane from lateral to medial and walked off the inferior articular process/transverse process into the paravertebral space, just deep to the superior costotransverse ligament.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: This muscle occupies the posterior part of the costotransverse region, running from a transverse process to the rib below (or two below, for the longer fascicles). The posterior approach to a thoracic paravertebral block (TPVB) passes through or immediately adjacent to it en route from the erector spinae mass to the paravertebral space, which lies just anterior to the superior costotransverse ligament.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: Transverse process and rib seen as hyperechoic structures with posterior acoustic shadowing; the paravertebral space is seen as a wedge-shaped hypoechoic area deep to the internal intercostal membrane, with the pleura sliding just below it.
structures_at_risk: pleura and lung (pneumothorax) -- the paravertebral space's anterior boundary
epidural space, since the paravertebral space communicates medially with it (risk of unexpectedly high or bilateral spread)
the segmental spinal nerve as it exits the intervertebral foramen
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: No motor-point/neural-arborization mapping for BoNT injection into this small muscle was found. What is genuinely documented is the posterior approach to the thoracic paravertebral block (TPVB), whose needle path runs through or immediately adjacent to this muscle en route to the paravertebral space -- included here as the real clinical 'injection approach' relevant to this muscle's anatomical location, not a claim of a direct intramuscular motor-point target.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Karmakar MK, Pakpirom J, Sivakumar RK, Samy W (2024) 'Ultrasound-guided thoracic paravertebral block using a transverse in-plane approach at the level of the inferior articular process: a retrospective review of complications', Reg Anesth Pain Med 49(10):770-772, doi:10.1136/rapm-2022-103983; Karmakar MK, Li X, Li J, Hadzic A (2012) 'Volumetric three-dimensional ultrasound imaging of the anatomy relevant for thoracic paravertebral block', Anesth Analg 115(5):1246-1250, doi:10.1213/ANE.0b013e318266c37d -- anatomic detail of the costotransverse/paravertebral region this muscle occupies
